current.text: He is Indiana's backup point guard. He is part of the bench rotation with Oubre, Toppin, Huff and Jarace Walker.
He should play about 17 to 19 minutes a night, whether or not Haliburton plays.
He is a streaming option for FG%, assists and steals, not a player to hold all season.
He is 35. The experts list his age as one of the questions on the Pacers roster.
With a season end of March 28, Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has 15 back-to-backs.
That playoff schedule is not ideal for a season that ends March 28.

durable.text: He shoots a very high field goal percentage, built on a very high two-point percentage. He has no three-point shot.
He has a very high steal rate and adds assists. His low minutes keep his per-game steals near the league average.
He is a ball-dominant guard. He led the league in on-ball percentage at about 48%.

note: Yahoo ranks him 231 and ESPN ranks him 190, and both value him at 0 USD. In a 12-team league that drafts 144 players, he should go undrafted, so do not spend auction money on him. He is a waiver streamer for FG%, assists and steals, and he costs little in turnovers. His FG% helps less than it looks because he takes only about 8 shots a game. He gives nothing in threes and little in points, rebounds or blocks. Early in the season, check that he keeps his 17 to 19 minutes as a 35-year-old. Then stream him in weeks when Indiana plays 4 games. In our playoffs Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games, so he is a weak option there.
